claims.text: The trip is outside tolerance, so the POL-RD-24 refund matrix is engaged. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation as the platform's recorded distances, actual minus recommended: 22.9 km minus 21.3 km = 1.60 km, against a tolerance of 1.0 km. A deviation of 1.60 km is over tolerance, which excludes rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 and puts the rider's claim on the refund side of the matrix.

The deviation is real and is the one the rider describes, so it is not a mapping or recording artifact. The platform's own event log records the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the PIE / Eng Neo Avenue exit at 08:12:19 and rejoining it only at the Bukit Timah Road / CTE slip road at 08:22:49, and the GPS trace shows the vehicle on Dunearn Road and then Bukit Timah Road across that 10 min 30 s window - precisely the roads the rider names in his claim. POL-RD-22 uses the trace for exactly this purpose: to show which route was taken and when.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on this record, so row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data shows an incident that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The LTA advisory is of the right type (ACCIDENT) and overlaps the trip window (07:44:37 to 08:54:37), but its own derived facts leave the decisive limb open: 'intersects_route' is null and the stated reason is that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'. The driver's assertion of an accident in the chat cannot fill that gap: POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. Row (d) refunds the excess distance fare in full.

In the alternative, even if the Judge finds the advisory intersects the recommended route, the case is not row (a): the driver has not established that he informed the rider 'before or at the point of deviation' as POL-RD-21 requires. The chat log is IMPAIRED - issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4 - because entry MSG-05011-003 carries a driver-device sent_at of 08:10:49 and a server delivered_at of 08:14:19, 210 seconds apart and falling on opposite sides of the route_deviation_detected event at 08:12:19. On the platform's own delivery record the message reached the rider only after the vehicle had already left the route, and the only timestamps that would place it before the turn are the driver's own device clock on the very entry the pre-pass found to be in conflict; the rider's account that he was not asked before the turn is therefore contradicted by no unimpaired timing. Row (b) refunds the excess distance fare.

The rider's reply 'ok can' at 08:14:39 does not turn this into the agreed deviation that row (a) rewards. POL-RD-21 ties the agreed deviation to an acknowledgment of a notice given 'before or at the point of deviation'; this reply came two minutes twenty seconds after the vehicle had left the recommended route, and after the trace shows it already running on Dunearn Road. At most it is acquiescence in a detour already under way, not the informed agreement on which NO_ACTION depends.

The money the policy provides is the excess distance fare and no more: POL-RD-24 defines it as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge - 1.60 km x 0.72 = 1.152 SGD, rounded to the cent at 1.15 SGD. The ledger records that the rider was charged 37.55 SGD and that refund_issued_sgd is still 0.00 with payment_status CHARGED, so the ruling should be PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.15 SGD, which is the whole of the excess distance fare POL-RD-24 provides for this deviation and leaves the rider not carrying it.

If the Judge instead finds that whether the driver notified the rider before or at the point of deviation cannot be settled on this record - and the chat log is impaired at weight_multiplier 0.4 with CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT on precisely that entry - then POL-GEN-02(2) caps the confidence available for that fact at 0.4, below the 0.80 that POL-GEN-22 requires for a 37.55 SGD dispute, and POL-GEN-26 names that very open question and sends the case to a human reviewer. On that footing the fare is held rather than collected; what the record cannot support is a NO_ACTION that leaves the rider carrying the charge on a notice the evidence cannot place before the turn.

No escalation is needed if the Judge takes row (d): the facts that decide it - the recorded distances and the traffic advisory - are carried by artifacts the pre-pass graded COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02(2) sets no cap below the 0.80 that POL-GEN-22 requires, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (absent on both, and so 0 under POL-GEN-22) to raise that bar to 0.95.

claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: POL-RD-22 measures it as trip_record.actual_distance_km 22.9 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 21.3 km = 1.60 km, which is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 therefore cannot apply, and the case must be decided on row (a), (b) or (d).

POL-RD-23's traffic justification is met. EV-ADVIS-05011-01 is an LTA traffic advisory of type ACCIDENT, and ACCIDENT is inside the policy's admissible 'incident' vocabulary; its road field is the Pan-Island Expressway (PIE), which is one of the roads the recommended route uses (trip_record.optimal_route_via: KJE, PIE, CTE, Outram Road); its validity window 07:44:37 to 08:54:37 brackets the whole trip window 07:54:37 to 08:29:07; and its own text directs drivers to avoid lanes 1 and 2 on PIE at that time, which is exactly why the driver left PIE. The record carries nothing putting this incident off the recommended route — the derived intersects_route field is returned null for the Judge rather than answered — and the driver's contemporaneous message to the rider (MSG-05011-003) describes the same PIE accident. On the road, type and window the artifact itself carries, the advisory intersects the recommended route.

The driver informed the rider of the deviation and the rider agreed to it. MSG-05011-003 reads 'Accident on PIE after Adam Rd, I exit Eng Neo and go Bukit Timah ok?' and MSG-05011-004 answers 'ok can'; POL-RD-21 makes that acknowledgment an agreed deviation. The rider's later claim that 'he did not ask me before turning' is contradicted by his own in-app reply. I disclose that EV-CHAT-05011 is IMPAIRED — weight_multiplier 0.4, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT — and the impairment goes only to which of that entry's two clocks is right, not to the words exchanged, which are identical on both sources.

The notice came before the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. The deviation is detected at 08:12:19 and the first Dunearn Road fix is at 08:12:07 (EV-TRIP-05011, EV-GPS-05011), while the driver-device timestamp on MSG-05011-003 is 08:10:49 and that same entry records read_at 08:11:13 — both before the turn. The 08:14:19 delivered_at is the lone outlier on that entry (the pre-pass notes every other entry agrees within 3 s, including this device's own MSG-05011-001 and MSG-05011-002, so a device-wide clock skew is excluded), and on the face of the entry a read receipt cannot post-date delivery by three minutes. The coherent reading of the entry is the device clock: notice before the deviation, with the rider's 'ok can' at 08:14:39 given while the vehicle was still on the diverted road (deviation rejoined 08:22:49). EV-CHAT-05011 is impaired — weight 0.4, CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT — and that is the issue I am asking the Judge to resolve, not to ignore.

The case fits POL-RD-24 row (a) — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — so the ruling is NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative, and on this record it is the driver's outcome: the rider is the filer, the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 (EV-FARE-05011), so leaving the present state standing leaves the metered charge exactly where it is and moves nothing back to the rider.

However the informing question falls, the matrix caps the money. The excess distance fare under POL-RD-24 is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.15 SGD (EV-FARE-05011, derived.money.excess_distance_fare_sgd). That single figure is the whole of what rows (b) and (d) return, and row (a) returns nothing; no row returns the trip fare, and the surge of 7.65 SGD and the time fare of 6.21 SGD are outside the excess-distance formula. The 37.55 SGD the rider claims as the full fare cannot be awarded in whole on any application of the clause.

The impairment on the chat log does not cap the whole case at 0.4. The fact that the driver messaged the rider in-trip and the rider answered is also carried by the trip record's own derived.messages_during_trip listing made under POL-RD-21 (MSG-05011-003 from the driver and MSG-05011-004 from the rider), and EV-TRIP-05011 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the weight for a fact two artifacts carry is read at the highest of them; the 0.4 attaches to EV-CHAT-05011 (issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT) and to the narrow question of which clock on one entry is right — it does not touch the deviation (EV-TRIP-05011, 1.0), the traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05011-01, 1.0) or the fare (EV-FARE-05011, 1.0).

Nothing here removes the case from the AI or raises the confidence bar. The contested amount is 37.55 SGD, inside POL-GEN-22's 10.00 to 50.00 SGD band where an AI ruling stands at 0.80 confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag; no safety indicator appears in a trip that ran to completion at 08:29:07; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not switched on (route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false) — and a 1.60 km deviation would sit under 2 km in any event. The artifacts carrying the deviation, the traffic advisory and the fare are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

ruling.explanation: Rider and driver: this dispute goes to a human reviewer, with the SGD 37.55 held rather than collected or refunded. The trip is 1.60 km longer than the recommended route - 22.9 km actually driven against 21.3 km recommended (EV-TRIP-05011) - which is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the POL-RD-24 refund matrix is engaged; both sides agree on that, and the GPS trace and event log confirm the vehicle left the PIE at the Eng Neo Avenue exit at 08:12:19 and rejoined at the Bukit Timah Road / CTE slip road at 08:22:49. I also find the reroute traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05011-01) is an ACCIDENT on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Changi after the Adam Road exit, valid 07:44:37 to 08:54:37, which overlaps the trip window and lies on the PIE stretch of the recommended route in the direction the trip was travelling; the driver's in-trip message describes the same incident. That removes rows (c), (d) and (e). The case therefore stands on row (a) or row (b), and both turn on one question: did the driver inform the rider before or at the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires? The record cannot settle that at the confidence this policy requires. The only artifact that speaks to it is the chat log EV-CHAT-05011, and the platform graded it impaired: weight_multiplier 0.4, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT. MSG-05011-003 carries a driver-device sent time of 08:10:49 - before the deviation - and a server delivery time of 08:14:19 - after it - so the same entry supports both readings, and the rider's reply 'ok can' (MSG-05011-004) is at 08:14:39 on either reading. The driver's account that he messaged before the exit, and the trip record's in-trip message list, do not cure this: POL-RD-21 reads the chat log, the statement is an account standing in for the conflicted timing rather than independent evidence, and the trip record's list repeats the same chat entry rather than measuring it separately, so it is not a second independent source under POL-GEN-02(2). Because the fact that decides between rows (a) and (b) is carried by an artifact at 0.4, POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at 0.4, below the 0.80 that POL-GEN-22 and POL-RD-25 require for a 37.55 SGD dispute. On the money: row (a) would leave the 37.55 SGD metered fare (EV-FARE-05011) standing, and row (b) would return only the excess distance fare - 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.15 SGD - and no more; no row returns the surge of 7.65 SGD, the time fare of 6.21 SGD, or any other part of the 37.55 SGD, so the full fare the rider asks for cannot be awarded. Neither row can be ruled at the required confidence, so under POL-GEN-26 the case is escalated for the open question - whether the notice preceded the turn - to be decided by a human reviewer. No safety flag and no fraud flag applies, so the escalation rests on POL-GEN-26 and POL-RD-25 alone. No referral is attached: the route-deviation policy contains no referral clause.

ruling.explanation:
This case goes to a human reviewer. The disputed fare of 37.55 SGD is held — not collected and not refunded — and no money moves in either direction.

What is settled. The ride was longer than the recommended route. On the platform's own recorded distances (EV-TRIP-05011, POL-RD-22): actual 22.9 km against recommended 21.3 km, a deviation of 1.60 km, above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05011) puts the vehicle on Dunearn Road and then Bukit Timah Road from about 08:12 to 08:22 — the roads the rider names — so the deviation is real and not a recording artifact. Both sides' claims on the deviation are accepted, and it puts the case outside the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24.

Traffic. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05011-01, POL-RD-23) is an ACCIDENT on the Pan-Island Expressway (towards Changi) after the Adam Road exit, valid 07:44:37–08:54:37, bracketing the trip window 07:54:37–08:29:07. The recommended route (EV-TRIP-05011) runs on the PIE, and the advisory sits on that road in the direction of travel, ahead of the point where the vehicle left it. The reroute is therefore traffic-justified, and POL-RD-24 row (d) is not available; the argument that it should apply because the advisory's derived 'intersects_route' field is blank is not accepted — the record leaves that call to the Judge, and on road, direction and location it falls on the recommended route.

The open question. Whether the driver gave notice of the deviation 'before or at the point of deviation' as POL-RD-21 requires cannot be established. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05011) is impaired: weight_multiplier 0.4, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT (POL-GEN-02). Entry MSG-05011-003 ('Accident on PIE after Adam Rd, I exit Eng Neo and go Bukit Timah ok?') carries a driver-device sent_at of 08:10:49 and a server delivered_at of 08:14:19 — 210 seconds apart and on opposite sides of the deviation detected at 08:12:19 — and its read_at of 08:11:13 cannot post-date delivery. The words exchanged are not in dispute and the rider's 'ok can' at 08:14:39 is accepted as his reply; what is undecided is whether the notice preceded the turn. Because that limb is impaired, it supports neither a payment that needs it to hold nor a refund that needs it to fail: row (a) (informed and agreed — no refund) and row (b) (rider not informed — refund) both fail on it, and row (d) is unavailable. The case fits no row, and POL-GEN-26 (v2.1 6.3) sends it to a human reviewer.

Independently, POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence in that fact at the weight of the artifact that carries it — 0.4 (EV-CHAT-05011) — which is below the 0.80 that POL-GEN-22 and POL-RD-25 (v2.1 6.2) require for a dispute of 37.55 SGD. The driver's argument that the trip record's derived.messages_during_trip carries the messaging fact independently at 1.0 is rejected: that listing restates the same chat measurement (same message ids, same device timestamps), so it is one carrier, not two, and cannot lift the 0.4 cap.

The arithmetic the parties agree on. Had row (b) or (d) applied, POL-RD-24's excess distance fare would be 1.60 km × 0.72 SGD/km = 1.15 SGD (EV-FARE-05011), without surge (the 7.65 SGD surge and the 6.21 SGD time fare are outside that formula), and the ledger shows the rider charged 37.55 SGD with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. No row returns the whole 37.55 SGD fare, and no figure is awarded here because the row cannot be determined.

No profile material was used to decide the trip (POL-GEN-01); neither profile carries a fraud flag and the value sits in POL-GEN-22's 10.00–50.00 SGD band, so the bar is 0.80, no safety flag applies, and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off. No referral arises: a route deviation has no referral clause in this version. What the reviewer should settle is the clock conflict on MSG-05011-003 — whether the notice reached the rider before or after the vehicle left the PIE.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this fare dispute cannot be decided on the record, so it goes to a human reviewer and the 37.55 SGD metered fare is held, not collected or refunded.

What is settled. The platform's own recorded distances give a deviation of 22.9 km minus 21.3 km = 1.60 km (EV-TRIP-05011), above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the POL-RD-24 matrix is engaged and the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) cannot apply. The trip events and the GPS trace confirm the vehicle really left the recommended route at the PIE / Eng Neo Avenue exit (08:12:19) and rejoined at the Bukit Timah Road / CTE slip road (08:22:49) — the Dunearn / Bukit Timah detour the rider describes.

The traffic point. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05011-01) is an ACCIDENT on the PIE, a road the recommended route uses, with a validity window (07:44-08:54) that covers the trip; read against the recommended route, the reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. That excludes row (d), so the refund side cannot be reached that way.

The undecided point. What remains is whether the driver informed the rider before or at the point of deviation, which POL-RD-21 requires and on which POL-RD-24 rows (a) and (b) both turn. That rests on one chat entry (EV-CHAT-05011, MSG-05011-003), which the pre-pass graded IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.4 with issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT: the driver-device sent_at 08:10:49 falls before the deviation event 08:12:19 and the server delivered_at 08:14:19 falls after it, 210 seconds apart. The trip record's message list only repeats the chat log's own timestamps, so it is not an independent source and does not resolve the conflict. The rider's 'ok can' reply at 08:14:39 is admitted, but it does not tell us when the notice arrived. The point is therefore undecided, and an undecided point supports neither a no-refund (row a) nor a refund (row b).

Why escalate. Under POL-RD-24 a case that fits no row is escalated under POL-GEN-26, and POL-GEN-26 names 'whether the driver notified the rider' as a fact that escalates when the evidence cannot establish it. POL-RD-25 independently bars an AI ruling: it requires confidence of at least 0.80, and the notice-timing fact is carried only by the impaired chat log at 0.4.

The money figures, so you both know where this stood. POL-RD-24's excess distance fare is 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.15 SGD (EV-FARE-05011), and no row of the matrix returns the 37.55 SGD metered fare, its 7.65 SGD surge or its 6.21 SGD time fare. That 1.15 SGD is not paid now.

Driver: your claim that you informed the rider and she agreed cannot be resolved at the required confidence, because the entry carrying it is impaired and the trip record does not corroborate it independently. Rider: your account that you were not asked before the turn is noted, but it cannot supply the timing the impaired log cannot, so it cannot ground the 1.15 SGD refund either. The question for the human reviewer is narrow: decide which clock on MSG-05011-003 is right — the device reading before the deviation or the server reading after it — and apply POL-RD-24 row (a) or row (b) accordingly.

ruling.explanation: Route deviation on TRP-05011 (DSP-05011). Outcome: the case goes to a human reviewer and the 37.55 SGD fare is held — not collected further and not refunded. To the rider: you are right about the deviation, and right that no application of this policy returns the whole fare. To the driver: you are right that the reroute was in response to a real incident, and right that no row returns the full 37.55 SGD — but the one fact that separates a no-refund from a refund cannot be settled on this record. Both sides agree, and the record confirms, the deviation: the platform's recorded distances are 22.9 km driven against a recommended 21.3 km, a deviation of 1.60 km (POL-RD-22), over the 1.0 km tolerance. That engages the POL-RD-24 matrix and excludes the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e). The matrix's money figure — the most either party could be awarded — is the excess distance fare, 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.15 SGD, without surge (POL-RD-24); the contested 37.55 SGD, the 7.65 SGD surge and the 6.21 SGD time fare lie outside that formula, and EV-FARE-05011 shows refund_issued_sgd is still 0.00. The LTA traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05011-01, LTA-TI-260828-9828, ACCIDENT on the PIE — a road the recommended route uses — valid 07:44:37 to 08:54:37, bracketing the trip window) makes the reroute traffic-justified under POL-RD-23, so rows (d)/(e) are out. That leaves rows (a) [no refund] and (b) [refund the excess], and both turn on one fact: whether the driver informed the rider before or at the point of deviation (POL-RD-21). That fact cannot be settled. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05011) is impaired — weight_multiplier 0.4, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT — because the driver's reroute message MSG-05011-003 carries a driver-device timestamp of 08:10:49 and a server delivery timestamp of 08:14:19, 210 seconds apart and on opposite sides of the deviation event at 08:12:19. The words exchanged are not in dispute; the timing — the very thing POL-RD-21 requires — is. The limb is therefore undecided, and an undecided limb supports neither row (a) (which needs the notice to have been given in time) nor row (b) (which needs it not to have been); the rider's argument for row (b), resting on the server delivery record alone, is rejected for the same reason the driver's argument for row (a), resting on the device clock alone, is rejected. The driver's answer to the rider's claim, that the messages_during_trip listing in the trip record carries the same fact at weight 1.0, does not move this: that listing is drawn from the same chat messages and merely restates the device clock, so it is not an independent carrier of the timing. The driver's own statement in his counterparty account does not carry it either — POL-RD-21 reads the chat log or a call recording, not a party's account. No row of POL-RD-24 fits, and POL-GEN-26 names this exact fact ('whether the driver notified the rider'); the confidence for any ruling on it is capped at the 0.4 weight of the only artifact carrying it, below the 0.80 that POL-GEN-22 and POL-RD-25 require for a 37.55 SGD dispute. The amount is held. No clause in the route-deviation category produces a referral, so none is made. The question for the human reviewer is whether the driver's in-app notice preceded the 08:12:19 deviation (MSG-05011-003, EV-CHAT-05011).

ledger.claim: The trip is outside tolerance, so the POL-RD-24 refund matrix is engaged. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation as the platform's recorded distances, actual minus recommended: 22.9 km minus 21.3 km = 1.60 km, against a tolerance of 1.0 km. A deviation of 1.60 km is over tolerance, which excludes rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 and puts the rider's claim on the refund side of the matrix.

The deviation is real and is the one the rider describes, so it is not a mapping or recording artifact. The platform's own event log records the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the PIE / Eng Neo Avenue exit at 08:12:19 and rejoining it only at the Bukit Timah Road / CTE slip road at 08:22:49, and the GPS trace shows the vehicle on Dunearn Road and then Bukit Timah Road across that 10 min 30 s window - precisely the roads the rider names in his claim. POL-RD-22 uses the trace for exactly this purpose: to show which route was taken and when.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on this record, so row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data shows an incident that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The LTA advisory is of the right type (ACCIDENT) and overlaps the trip window (07:44:37 to 08:54:37), but its own derived facts leave the decisive limb open: 'intersects_route' is null and the stated reason is that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'. The chat log is IMPAIRED - issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4 - because entry MSG-05011-003 carries a driver-device sent_at of 08:10:49 and a server delivered_at of 08:14:19, 210 seconds apart and falling on opposite sides of the route_deviation_detected event at 08:12:19. On the platform's own delivery record the message reached the rider only after the vehicle had already left the route, and the only timestamps that would place it before the turn are the driver's own device clock on the very entry the pre-pass found to be in conflict; the rider's account that he was not asked before the turn is therefore contradicted by no unimpaired timing. Row (b) refunds the excess distance fare.

The rider's reply 'ok can' at 08:14:39 does not turn this into the agreed deviation that row (a) rewards. POL-RD-21 ties the agreed deviation to an acknowledgment of a notice given 'before or at the point of deviation'; this reply came two minutes twenty seconds after the vehicle had left the recommended route, and after the trace shows it already running on Dunearn Road. At most it is acquiescence in a detour already under way, not the informed agreement on which NO_ACTION depends.

ledger.claim: The money the policy provides is the excess distance fare and no more: POL-RD-24 defines it as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge - 1.60 km x 0.72 = 1.152 SGD, rounded to the cent at 1.15 SGD. The ledger records that the rider was charged 37.55 SGD and that refund_issued_sgd is still 0.00 with payment_status CHARGED, so the ruling should be PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.15 SGD, which is the whole of the excess distance fare POL-RD-24 provides for this deviation and leaves the rider not carrying it.

If the Judge instead finds that whether the driver notified the rider before or at the point of deviation cannot be settled on this record - and the chat log is impaired at weight_multiplier 0.4 with CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT on precisely that entry - then POL-GEN-02(2) caps the confidence available for that fact at 0.4, below the 0.80 that POL-GEN-22 requires for a 37.55 SGD dispute, and POL-GEN-26 names that very open question and sends the case to a human reviewer. On that footing the fare is held rather than collected; what the record cannot support is a NO_ACTION that leaves the rider carrying the charge on a notice the evidence cannot place before the turn.

No escalation is needed if the Judge takes row (d): the facts that decide it - the recorded distances and the traffic advisory - are carried by artifacts the pre-pass graded COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02(2) sets no cap below the 0.80 that POL-GEN-22 requires, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (absent on both, and so 0 under POL-GEN-22) to raise that bar to 0.95.

The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: POL-RD-22 measures it as trip_record.actual_distance_km 22.9 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 21.3 km = 1.60 km, which is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The within-tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 therefore cannot apply, and the case must be decided on row (a), (b) or (d).

POL-RD-23's traffic justification is met. EV-ADVIS-05011-01 is an LTA traffic advisory of type ACCIDENT, and ACCIDENT is inside the policy's admissible 'incident' vocabulary; its road field is the Pan-Island Expressway (PIE), which is one of the roads the recommended route uses (trip_record.optimal_route_via: KJE, PIE, CTE, Outram Road); its validity window 07:44:37 to 08:54:37 brackets the whole trip window 07:54:37 to 08:29:07; and its own text directs drivers to avoid lanes 1 and 2 on PIE at that time, which is exactly why the driver left PIE. The record carries nothing putting this incident off the recommended route — the derived intersects_route field is returned null for the Judge rather than answered — and the driver's contemporaneous message to the rider (MSG-05011-003) describes the same PIE accident. On the road, type and window the artifact itself carries, the advisory intersects the recommended route.

ledger.claim: The driver informed the rider of the deviation and the rider agreed to it. MSG-05011-003 reads 'Accident on PIE after Adam Rd, I exit Eng Neo and go Bukit Timah ok?' and MSG-05011-004 answers 'ok can'; POL-RD-21 makes that acknowledgment an agreed deviation. The rider's later claim that 'he did not ask me before turning' is contradicted by his own in-app reply. I disclose that EV-CHAT-05011 is IMPAIRED — weight_multiplier 0.4, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT — and the impairment goes only to which of that entry's two clocks is right, not to the words exchanged, which are identical on both sources.

The notice came before the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. The deviation is detected at 08:12:19 and the first Dunearn Road fix is at 08:12:07 (EV-TRIP-05011, EV-GPS-05011), while the driver-device timestamp on MSG-05011-003 is 08:10:49 and that same entry records read_at 08:11:13 — both before the turn. The 08:14:19 delivered_at is the lone outlier on that entry (the pre-pass notes every other entry agrees within 3 s, including this device's own MSG-05011-001 and MSG-05011-002, so a device-wide clock skew is excluded), and on the face of the entry a read receipt cannot post-date delivery by three minutes. The coherent reading of the entry is the device clock: notice before the deviation, with the rider's 'ok can' at 08:14:39 given while the vehicle was still on the diverted road (deviation rejoined 08:22:49). EV-CHAT-05011 is impaired — weight 0.4, CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT — and that is the issue I am asking the Judge to resolve, not to ignore.

The case fits POL-RD-24 row (a) — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — so the ruling is NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative, and on this record it is the driver's outcome: the rider is the filer, the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 (EV-FARE-05011), so leaving the present state standing leaves the metered charge exactly where it is and moves nothing back to the rider.

However the informing question falls, the matrix caps the money. The excess distance fare under POL-RD-24 is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.15 SGD (EV-FARE-05011, derived.money.excess_distance_fare_sgd). That single figure is the whole of what rows (b) and (d) return, and row (a) returns nothing; no row returns the trip fare, and the surge of 7.65 SGD and the time fare of 6.21 SGD are outside the excess-distance formula. The 37.55 SGD the rider claims as the full fare cannot be awarded in whole on any application of the clause.

The impairment on the chat log does not cap the whole case at 0.4. The fact that the driver messaged the rider in-trip and the rider answered is also carried by the trip record's own derived.messages_during_trip listing made under POL-RD-21 (MSG-05011-003 from the driver and MSG-05011-004 from the rider), and EV-TRIP-05011 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the weight for a fact two artifacts carry is read at the highest of them; the 0.4 attaches to EV-CHAT-05011 (issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT) and to the narrow question of which clock on one entry is right — it does not touch the deviation (EV-TRIP-05011, 1.0), the traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05011-01, 1.0) or the fare (EV-FARE-05011, 1.0).

Nothing here removes the case from the AI or raises the confidence bar. The contested amount is 37.55 SGD, inside POL-GEN-22's 10.00 to 50.00 SGD band where an AI ruling stands at 0.80 confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag; no safety indicator appears in a trip that ran to completion at 08:29:07; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not switched on (route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false) — and a 1.60 km deviation would sit under 2 km in any event. The artifacts carrying the deviation, the traffic advisory and the fare are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0.
